description_full: ZIM Integrated Shipping Services Ltd., together with its subsidiaries, provides container shipping and related services in Israel and internationally. The company offers door-to-door and port-to-port transportation services for various types of customers, including end-users, consolidators, and freight forwarders. It also provides ZIMonitor, a reefer cargo tracking service, a device attached to the engine of the reefer, and allows customers to track and monitor, cargo, such as pharmaceuticals, food and delicate electronics. As of December 31, 2025, it operated a fleet of 128 vessels, such as 115 container vessels and 13 vehicle transport vessels, as well as a network of 56 weekly lines. ZIM Integrated Shipping Services Ltd. was incorporated in 1945 and is headquartered in Haifa, Israel.

financial_summary: ZIM Integrated Shipping Service is a mid-cap industrials business with a $3.4B market cap on $6.9B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -18% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 111% against a 10% cost of capital — a 101-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 27%.

The business throws off $2.1B in free cash flow — roughly 30 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 4.78× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -16.5% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 2.1× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 15.3% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.
